definition: an opening in a wall or roof fitted with glass to let in light and air
hook: A window used to have no glass in it at all.
modernAnchor: We build entire walls of it now, floor-to-ceiling glass we still just call windows.
journey: Norse longhouses cut a hole in the roof to let smoke escape and light in.
There was no glass, so cold wind poured in through the same gap the light did.
Norse speakers called that gap vindauga, wind eye, since it stared back at the weather.
English borrowed the word centuries before anyone thought to fill the hole with glass.
